player.$comment: Movement states (step 3.1, spec §6.2). Speed = walkSpeed x (sprintMultiplier | sneakMultiplier | 1) x terrain rule x world.moveMultiplier x limp.
player.$metresPerPixel: the 48 px player sprite is about 1.9 m tall; distance travelled is reported in metres on the game-over screen

hydration.$comment: Hydration 0..max (spec §6.2). Drains slowly, faster while sprinting (running costs water: keeps sprinting a choice on long trips); rain in a squall refills it at rainPerSecond x squall intensity. Below staminaCapBelow (30) max stamina is staminaCapFraction (50%). At zero, health drops at thirstDamagePerSecond. From full: 100 -> 30 in 583 s (9.7 min), -> 0 in 833 s (13.9 min), dead of thirst 200 s later (17.2 min without a drink or rain).

health.$comment: Health 0..max (spec §6.2, §8). An arrow hit (M4) deals arrowDamage (50) plus a bleed of bleedDamagePerSecond for bleedSeconds (stopped by any heal) and a limp (speed x limpMultiplier) for limpSeconds: two arrows kill. Swimming at zero stamina drowns at drowningDamagePerSecond: from full stamina a swimmer has 40 s, then 12.5 s more.

stamina.$comment: Stamina 0..max (spec §6.2). Drains while sprinting and while swimming; regenerates when walking or still (faster when still) after regenDelaySeconds without exertion. A sprint starts only at sprintStartMin or more (no flicker at zero). 100 / 10 = 10 s of sprint from full; 100 / 2.5 = 40 s of swimming before drowning starts.

noise.$comment: Noise radius in world px by surface and action (spec §6.1: crouch on sand/water 20, walk on sand 60, walk in jungle brush 100, sprint 180, thrown impact 220); the gaps are filled to the same scale. 'water' is wading (shallow water, flooded ground); 'swim' is swimming (crouch and sprint cannot happen there; 'still' is treading water). Footsteps are multiplied by world.noiseMultiplier (a squall halves them); thrown impacts are not. loudAt: a noise this big or bigger raises noise_loud and is drawn as a faint ring. memorySeconds: how long the AI can still hear a noise after its last emission.

cover.$comment: Crouched inside a cover prop's coverRadius (tall grass, mangrove roots): enemy sight range against the player x visibilityFactor (0.35 = 65% less, spec §6.1); the sprite is drawn at spriteAlpha.

footprints.$comment: Prints on wet sand (spec §6.1): one every `spacing` px travelled on foot, gone after lifetimeSeconds (15 s), at most `max` kept.

props.$comment: sway: top-of-sprite lean in px at full wind (0 or absent = rigid); swayPush: tall grass leaning away from a passing player; light: a light the renderer adds at the prop (src/engine/Lighting.js: radius px, intensity 0..1, color, flicker 0..1, pulse { speed rad/s, depth 0..1 }, glow 0..1 additive colour, zoneBoost x anomaly strength)
props.$comment2: flat: a ground decal, drawn before the y-sorted upright scene and without a shadow (src/engine/Renderer.js); autoVariant: props the map gives no variant to take a stable one from their position (0-2, the sheet's <kind>_2/_3 when it has them). Neither changes the simulation.

swayPush.$comment: extra lean px away from a player within radius px

world.$comment: WorldState (src/world/WorldState.js): tide clock, day/night and weather. Seconds are real seconds.

tide.$startPhase: 0 = low water, 0.5 = high water. 0.7 = falling past mid-tide (height 0.65): the reef tip starts to emerge within the first minute and low water comes 108 s into a new game

day.$lengthSeconds: 13 minutes = 2.17 tide cycles: low water comes about 1.8 in-game hours later each day, so it drifts through day and night over successive days (720 s would pin it to the same hours); 25-40 minute runs last 2-3 days

visibility.$comment: src/world/visibility.js ambientVisibility: sight-range factor; night = moonless clear night, moonGain per unit of world.moonlight

weather.$firstSquallSeconds: fixed, so a new game's sky never depends on the seed; the first squall arrives after the first low water
weather.$squallSeconds: about one squall every 6-7 minutes (two per in-game day), raining a quarter of the time

lighting.$comment: src/engine/Lighting.js (presentation). ambient: keyframes by hour, linearly interpolated (colour and darkness = alpha of the tint layer); colours from assets/src/palette.gpl. moonLift: darkness removed per unit of world.moonlight. storm: blended in by world.weatherIntensity. resolution: lighting canvas size as a fraction of the logical view; smooth: scale it up with smoothing.

player.$comment: the small awareness light that keeps the character visible at night

weatherFx.$comment: src/engine/WeatherFx.js (presentation): rain in screen space, counts at full squall intensity; speeds in logical px/s

water.$comment: src/world/water.js depth classes from tide height h and a tile's flood threshold t: flooded (h > t) is shallow (wading) while h - t <= deepMargin, deep (swimming) beyond it: one rule (water.js isDeepFlood) for movement, rendering and the audits; 0.15 is the audited value (the reef tide gate was measured with it); not flooded but t - h <= wetMargin is wet (about to flood or just drained). frameMs: water animation fallback when the sheet has no tag.

inventory.$comment: src/entities/Inventory.js: the 6-slot hotbar is the whole inventory (spec §6.4). startingKit: what a new game carries. dropLongPressMs: holding a hotbar slot this long on touch drops its stack.

interaction.$comment: src/entities/Interactable.js. radius: world px from the player within which each action can be used (default for the rest). aimPickRadius: a click or tap within this of an in-range interactable picks it. spring: drinking channel length and hydration per second. gridCell: bucket size of the spatial lookup.

throw.$comment: src/entities/Projectile.js, thrown distractions (spec §3.2, §6.1). speed px/s; maxRange px (aim points beyond are clamped); defaultDistance: a throw without an aim point, in the facing direction; minAimDistance: a coconut (which is drunk on use) is thrown only when aimed at least this far; arcHeight: drawn peak height per px of distance, capped at maxArcHeight; radius: body of a landed item for the free-spot search; marchStep/backoff/landSearch px: line-of-sight sampling, step back from an obstacle, search for a free spot.

audit.$comment: The map audit (tools/audit/map.mjs, TASKS.md V2). Tools only: the game never reads this block. Distances in world px, times in s, areas in tiles.
audit.$reachRadius: an entity counts as reached when a cell the player can stand on is within this many px of it
audit.$tideGatedRegions: things here (and on any ground that floods) may be cut off at high tide; everything must still be walkable at low tide
audit.$seaMarkers: places out at sea, checked by the boat route instead of on foot
audit.$anchors: with the region anchors: every pair must be joined by two routes that share no tile (a patrol can never wall the player in); other places with a single way in are listed as warnings
audit.$chokeWidthTiles: min-cut widths are measured up to this many tiles; narrower borders and legs are listed
audit.$significantChokeTiles: a width-1 chokepoint matters when it cuts off at least this much walkable area

swimGate.$margin: at high tide the shortest unbroken swim to the target must exceed margin x a full stamina bar of swimming

provisional.$comment: PROVISIONAL until step 3.1 / 3.3 / 4.1 land: the audit reads tuning.stamina { max, swimDrainPerSecond }, tuning.hydration { max, decayPerSecond, staminaCapBelow } when they exist and falls back to these; tuning.ai.patrolSpeed (step 4.1) replaces the patrolSpeed that stood here. Stamina numbers are those of the step 3.1 branch (100 / 2.5 = 40 s of swimming per bar).

hydration.$decayPerSecond: the player agent's figures: thirst caps stamina after ~9.7 min (70 / 0.12 = 583 s) and empties at ~13.9 min

ai.$comment: The Sentinelese scouts (src/entities/SentineleseAI.js, spec §7.3, steps 4.1-4.3). Distances in world px, speeds px/s, times s. The player walks 60 and sprints 105.
ai.$patrolSpeed: slower than the player's walk: a patrol can be shadowed and overtaken; the map audit's loop times use it

lod.$comment: scouts within nearRadius of the player (or busy) run the full AI; beyond farRadius a patrolling scout is moved along its route by distance only (hysteresis between the two). 700 is well off screen (the view is about 480 x 270).

spawn.$comment: one scout per map scout entity, plus one more on routes with a one-way length of 3000 px or more (8 of the 29 routes): 37 scouts, spread evenly along their route

sight.$range: in clear daylight, standing in the open: most of the half-screen ahead; the night (x0.45, up to x0.66 with a full moon) and squalls (x0.7) shorten it, cover cuts it to 70
sight.$coneCos: cos of the cone's half-angle: 55 degrees (a 110 degree field of view); dot products only, never an angle
sight.$presenceRadius: all-round: a body this close is noticed whatever the facing (x cover, crouch and Resonance, not light)
sight.$crouchFactor: crouched in the open (not in cover): 30% shorter sight range against the player
sight.$alertRangeMultiplier: a scout in WARN, CHASE or SEARCH looks harder
sight.$flashlightVisibility: a lit flashlight: the light factor is at least this (a torch at night gives the player away)

awareness.$comment: meter 0..1; fill per second while in sight = fillPerSecond x (1 + closeBonus x (1 - d/range)) x (centralMin + (1 - centralMin) x centrality) [x alertFillMultiplier when hunting]. At the cone's edge and full range about 5 s to notice; half range, dead ahead 1 s; point blank 0.7 s. suspicious: INVESTIGATE the glimpse (question bubble); 1: seen (WARN or CHASE).

hearing.$comment: a noise whose radius reaches the scout (spec §6.1 radii) sets a point of interest, off by up to uncertaintyPx x (1 - strength) for a faint one; footsteps add stepsPerSecond x strength, an impact impactGain, never past cap (hearing alone never makes a sighting)

footprints.$comment: prints younger than footprints.lifetimeSeconds (15 s), in the cone within sightRange and in a clear line, are followed, freshest first, hop by hop up to trailStep apart

patrol.$comment: pauses at a ping-pong route's ends, and at a fifth of the other waypoints (fixed per scout and waypoint), with a look-round sweep of eighth-turns

search.$comment: after 6 s without line of sight: the last known position, aheadPx further the way the player went, and the nearest cover props and trunks (stood behind) within spotRadius, for at most `seconds`

warn.$comment: spec §7.3: shout (exclaim), draw (warn_bow), a warning arrow shortPx in front of the player, then the 3 s de-escalation window: the distance grown by backoffMargin, or out of sight, lowers the bow (lower_bow, eye) for watchSeconds; closing in by advanceMargin, or the window running out, is CHASE. No second warning for memorySeconds.

chase.$speed: faster than the player's walk (60), slower than a sprint (105): breaking away costs stamina
chase.$whistleRadius: spec §7.3: every scout within 300 px of the whistler joins the chase
chase.$loseSightSeconds: spec §7.3: line of sight broken for 6 s, then SEARCH

arrow.$comment: lethal shots: aimed at the player's position + velocity x flight time x leadFactor, then a uniform lateral error of +-(baseError + errorPerPx x d + errorPerCrossSpeed x crossing speed + darkError x (1 - light) + coverError in cover); a hit is player.applyArrowHit (health.arrowDamage 50 HP + bleed + limp: two hits kill). Every shot is telegraphed by drawSeconds of warn_bow, none before firstShotSeconds of a chase, at most maxShooters drawing at once. hitRadius is added to the player's body radius.
arrow.$staggerSeconds: a scout may start drawing only this long after any other scout did: two bows never loose together
arrow.$hitHoldSeconds: and the hunters stand and watch for this long (lower_bow): the wounded, limping player's one chance to break away
arrow.$driveOffAfterHit: when the hold ends, a hunter whose wounded quarry has kept running (farther by warn.backoffMargin, or out of sight) lowers its bow and lets it go (warn_end driven_off, the warning memory set): they defend their home, they do not finish off the fleeing
arrow.$hitGraceSeconds: after a hit nobody starts a draw for this long: a wounded (limping) player gets a chance to break away

path.$comment: arriveSlack: a goal a body cannot quite stand on (a waypoint against a trunk) counts as reached within this once the scout stops making progress. Bounded A* (src/world/pathfind.js): a window of the start/goal box + windowMargin tiles (at most maxWindow a side), maxNodes per search, nodesPerTick shared by all scouts; wading tiles cost wadePenalty px extra

zones.$comment: where the player is seen decides warning or attack: inland regions are attacked without a warning; coastal ones (and any region not listed as inland) get the warning

threat.$comment: sim.threat and the HUD's eye summarise the scouts within this of the player

dialogue.$comment: Step 4.5, the dialogue box (src/ui/DialogueUI.js). Sizes in logical pixels unless named Css (CSS pixels, converted with the viewport scale like tuning.input). cps: typewriter characters per second; pauseMs: extra pause after . , ? ! and the dash.

marek.$comment: Step 4.5. radius: body (the player cannot walk through him); standHours: [from, to) in-game hours he stands (idle) instead of sitting: fishing at first light and at dusk.

safeZones.$comment: Step 4.5. Circles where scouts never go and never pursue (step 4.1) and where the autosave triggers (5.2): { id, landmark, radius } centred on a map landmark, or { id, x, y, radius }.

resonance.$comment: src/world/Resonance.js (spec §6.3). Target = min(max, sum of sources) x (1 - totemDampening if a Driftwood Totem is carried); the value walks to it at riseRate / fallRate points per second. Tiers: up at hummingAt / agitatedAt, down only hysteresis points below. Sources in points: flashlight while on, electronicEach per other electronic item powered on, anomalyAtFull x anomaly zone strength (0..1) where the player stands, monolith.near x (1 - distance / monolith.radius px) for the nearest monolith. detectionMultiplier: scout detection radius factor per tier. pulse: each anomaly zone pulses every baseSeconds + (1 - strength) x weakExtraSeconds, divided by (1 + speedAtMax x value / max).

resonanceFx.$comment: src/engine/ResonanceFx.js and src/ui/hud/Compass.js (presentation). intensity: comfort scale for every screen effect, 0 disables them (the compass and bar stay). vignette alpha by tier, pulsing at pulseSpeed rad/s. distortion: Agitated only, a brief channel-split pulse every everySeconds[0] at 70 down to everySeconds[1] at 100, lasting pulseSeconds, offset px, alpha. ring: the expanding ring of an anomaly pulse (seconds, radius px, line width px). monolith: monolith lights within sightRadius px of the player brighten by boost x value / 100. compass: needle jitter amplitude (rad) across Humming, spin speed (rad/s) at 70 and at 100.

fog.$comment: src/world/FogOfWar.js. The explored map at one cell per cellTiles x cellTiles tiles. sightRadius px around the player is revealed, times ambientVisibility (night, squall) but never below minSightRadius, times highGround.multiplier in highGround.regions. landmarkRevealRadius: what revealLandmarks() uncovers around each landmark. shifting (Shifting Paths, spec §6.3): while Resonance is Agitated and the player is inside an anomaly zone or in one of shifting.regions, only memoryRadius px are kept and cells between memoryRadius and forgetRadius are forgotten.

mapOverlay.$comment: src/ui/MapOverlay.js (presentation). The island cache is one pixel per tile, built chunkRows rows per frame. zoomLevels: map pixels per tile on screen as multiples of the fit-to-screen scale. panSpeed: logical px/s with the keys.

story.$comment: src/entities/storyInteractions.js (step 4.7). repairSeconds: patching the dinghy (a channel: moving or pressing again stops it, nothing spent). prySeconds: prying the wreck's hatch with the crowbar, which makes a noise of pryNoiseRadius world px every tick (louder than a sprint, 180, and a thrown rock, 220). flareGunRounds: flares loaded in the wreck's gun; flarePouchRounds: the Cartographer's pouch. signalRadius: world px from the signal point within which the flare gun may be fired (anywhere else it refuses, so it is never wasted).

lore.$comment: src/sim/Lore.js (step 4.6). visitRadius: world px; a landmark already discovered from a found map gets its discovery note once the player comes this close.

journal.$comment: src/ui/JournalUI.js (presentation, step 4.6). Logical pixels unless named Css (CSS pixels, converted with the viewport scale). fontPx/lineHeight: body text; titlePx: entry titles; tabHeight: the tab row on desktop, touchTabCss the least it is on a touch screen; rowHeight / touchRowCss: list rows; listWidth: fraction of the content for the Notes list (min..max px); wheelStep / keyStep: px scrolled per wheel notch / key press; mapKeyPan: px per arrow press on the Map tab.
